instrument: d11 flip instrument: (a) a probe that issues anonymous MCP tools/call for every dashboards tool that traverses DASHBOARDS_BACKEND_URL, through the live hauska-mcp-server; (b) a comparator that decides MATCH on semantics with a declared, proven exclusion set; (c) a log differential on the GCP original as an independent origin witness. Not scripts/surface-probe.mjs: that instrument is OPS-23's completion predicate (P-151..P-175, P-241) plus an OPS-24 customer leg (P-254) and carries no D-row predicate, and the close gate's GATED_ROW tests /^P-(\d+)$/ against GATED_RANGES [[151,174],[186,198],[200,250],[252,320]], so a D-row close is out of that gate's scope by construction. Citing a surface-probe artifact here would assert a provenance that does not exist.
whyRawBytesAreNotTheVerdict: Two consecutive pre-flip runs return identical byte counts with different raw hashes. The only difference is two build stamps the dashboards backend writes into every response: assertedAt and assembledAt. A raw-hash verdict would have reported a clean flip as a failure.

instrumentSelfTest.how: The comparator was run against two pre-flip runs (preA vs preB), where every row must MATCH.
instrumentSelfTest.firstVersionFailed: Its first version reported 3 DIVERGED, because it searched for unescaped keys inside the MCP text envelope where the backend JSON is escaped. Unwrapping the envelope fixed it. The instrument was corrected before it was trusted.

Observed behaviourally at the end: the original's /api/ log shows MCP-server calls during the pre-flip baseline (20:44:45, 20:45:12-20:45:15) and my positive control at 20:51:32, then NOTHING after -- so the live surface has stopped calling it, which is the intended effect, not a mutation.

originWitness.why: A semantic MATCH cannot by itself prove the flip took effect: the DO backend serves the same content, so identical output is expected either way. The GCP original's own request log is the independent witness that the canary and the live surface stopped calling it.
originWitness.instrumentName: Cloud Run request logs on service smartcity-dashboards, project smartcity-dashboards

scratch.text: A service whose traffic is PINNED to a revision by name does not cut over on a config-only redeploy. gcloud run deploy created the new revision, reported 'revision [OLD] has been deployed and is serving 100 percent of traffic' -- a true statement about the OLD revision -- while the new revision got 0% and Cloud Run retired it (Active=False, reason=Retired). The flip was configured but not live. Read the SERVING revision and the traffic split, never the deploy message.

Byte-identical payloads do not prove a backend flip. Both backends serve the same content, so a MATCH is satisfied either way. Prove a backend change with an independent witness on the origin you are leaving: after the flip the GCP original logged zero calls while a positive control on the same instrument logged one.

The dashboards backend stamps assertedAt and assembledAt into every response, so a raw-hash before/after comparison reports a clean flip as a failure. Declare the exclusion set, and prove it complete by locating every ISO instant in the payload and checking it sits under a declared key.

On this fleet host Node's bundled CA store rejects every TLS leaf because a proxy re-signs them ('unable to verify the first certificate'), while curl.exe succeeds from the Windows store. Run node with --use-system-ca. The hauska-mcp-server repo documents the same corporate-root condition for npm installs.

doctl is NOT authenticated on this host (no token; `doctl account get` fails). D-9 had a DO agent token and the fleet preamble says doctl and the DO MCP servers are configured fleet-wide, but not in this session. DO-side logs were therefore unavailable and the GCP original's logs were used as the origin witness instead.

gcloud run services update --update-env-vars changes config but does NOT move traffic; with traffic pinned it would have been a silent no-op. gcloud run deploy does move traffic, but only to a revision it is allowed to serve -- this service's pinned traffic meant the new revision was retired instead.
gcloud logging read with two OR-ed clauses in one filter returned exit 1; the single-term filter httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/lenses" works.
PowerShell's Set-Content -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM that makes JSON.parse throw 'Unexpected token'. Strip it.
